newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia 1996 Riga airport turnover up slightly.
newsitem.headline: Latvia 1996 Riga airport turnover up slightly.

text.p: Passenger turnover at the airport of Latvia's capital city, Riga, rose one percent to 497,124 in 1996 from 490,607 in 1995, officials said on Monday.
The rise was well below a planned five or seven percent gain, airport manager Dzintar Pomers told a news conference.
He also said cargo turnover has been stable for three years at around some 4,000 tonnes a year, way below the Soviet-era peaks during the late 1980s.
Riga airport was transformed from a state company into a state joint stock company with shares last month.

Pomers said a smaller percentage of passengers flying through the airport last year were destined for CIS countries at 17 percent against 21 percent in 1995. Last year's remaining 83 percent of passengers are listed as flying to the West.
A new passenger terminal is also planned at an estimated cost of $15 million, most of which will be borrowed. The runway is also to be extended to 3.2 kms from 2.5 kms.
"We have plenty of loan offers both from Western institutions and Latvian banks," Pomers said.
"Our operating income is not enough to finance it and we will introduce a departure tax of around seven lats or $15," Pomers said.
A tender for the loan is expected to be announced in a month or two months time, when a repayment plan has been drawn up. - Martinsh Gravitis, Riga Newsroom + 371 721 5240
